newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEONARD IS HANDED KEMPER TITLE BY WIEBE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEONARD IS HANDED KEMPER TITLE BY WIEBE.

text.p: Justin Leonard was handed a one-stroke victory at the Kemper Open when Mark Wiebe self-destructed with bogeys on the final two holes Sunday.
Leonard shot a closing four-under-par 67 on the Avenel TPC course and then watched as the third round leader Wiebe fell apart on the 17th and 18th holes.
Wiebe missed from inside two feet at the 17th to fall back into a tie and then three-putted on the last hole, missing a three-footer for par that he needed to make to force a play-off.
After claiming his second career tour victory and the $270,000 first place check, Leonard sympathised with Weibe's collapse that featured three bogeys on the final four holes.
"It feels great to win but I would rather have gone into a playoff and won that way," said the 24-year-old Leonard, who finished at 10-under 274.

Wiebe shot 73 to finish second on 275, while the high powered threesome of former major winners Nick Faldo (71), Greg Norman (67) and Nick Price (67) shared third along with Mike Springer (72) in the final tune-up for the US Open that starts at nearby Congressional on Thursday.
Wiebe started the final round with a three-shot lead and looked to be ready to win for the first time in 11 years when he increased his cushion to four shots after six holes.
But he started to stumble with a bogey at the eighth, the first of four three-putts in the final 11 holes.
"I can't believe it," said Wiebe, who is taking two injections a week to control his allergic reaction to several types of trees and grasses.
"When you hit putts like that it's not to be," said Wiebe. "I've been shaky over my short putts all week. Today maybe it caught up with me. Even the putts I made my hands felt a little quivery."
